title: Dry-spell age matching retained an 8% post-1997 recession rise in 348 southern Australian catchments
abstract: We test whether a change in dry-spell age explains faster stream recession after 1997. We use CAMELS-AUS v2.03 daily flow and AGCD and SILO rain. We match flow bins, season and dry-spell age, with a within-cell flow correction. In 348 southern catchments, the pooled 1997-2021 increase relative to 1951-1996 is 8.0% with AGCD (conditional 95% spatial interval 5.4-10.7%) and 8.3% with SILO (5.6-11.3%). Age matching changes the log effect by only -0.010 and -0.008. Thus dry-spell age does not explain the full pooled rise. But direct estimates for spells of at least eight dry days and for 2010-2021 are only about 1-3%, with intervals across zero. Paired common-catchment contrasts confirm smaller estimates in these subsets. An earlier long-spell slowdown makes the post-minus-placebo contrast positive, so reference era matters. The north has slower recessions. The work strengthens the pooled observation but does not establish a persistent faster slow-store drainage process or identify the physical cause. Intervals hold years and support fixed. Source rights, exact hashes, code, catchment statistics, all spatial samples, figure and numerical audit are supplied.

display.caption: Recession changes with and without dry-spell age matching. Bars are conditional 95% spatial intervals. The long-spell and later-period direct estimates are uncertain. The placebo subtraction uses a different reference era.

citations.reason: We test dry-spell age with raw daily records. The pooled increase remains, but later-period and long-spell direct estimates are uncertain.
Flow signatures alone do not identify a physical loss process.
